newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks seen banking on HSBC rally.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks seen banking on HSBC rally.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks may break new records in the coming week on renewed interest in HSBC Holdings and Hong Kong Telecom, but technical indicators suggest the market is overdue for a correction, brokers said.
"Why not buy HSBC Holdings instead of red chips," said Carlton Poon, research director at Worldsec International. "It has been behaving like a (small capitalised) second line stock."

The Hang Seng Index vaulted 190.50 points, or 1.39 percent, to a record close of 13,930.80 on Friday. The index also set an all-time intra-day high of 14,047.20, smashing the previous record of 14,004.93, set on January 16 this year.
Over the week, the index gained 849.10 points, or 6.49 percent, due to a partial shift of investor interest back to solid blue chips, chiefly HSBC Holdings, brokers said.
Turnover, which had been heavy throughout the week, also hit a record of HK$17.85 billion on Friday. This brought average daily turnover during the week to HK$15.39 billion.
Renewed interest in London and Hong Kong in banking giant HSBC Holdings catapulted the share to new highs last week.
HSBC rose to HK$217.00 on Friday from last week's close of HK$197.50, or a gain of 9.87 percent.
"We have a target of HK$280.00 for the bank for end 1997," said Poon.
Demand for HSBC and for red chips will fuel the index's rise to 20,000 by the end of 1997 or early 1998, he added.

In the coming week, investors will also be pondering the future of Hong Kong Telecommunications, following the sale by CITIC Pacific of its 7.75 percent stake in the telecoms company to Beijing-based China Everbright Holdings Ltd, a move which was announced on Friday.
The market viewed the deal as positive for CITIC Pacific, which closed HK$0.90 higher at HK$44.40 on Friday.
Hongkong Telecom, which had languished below HK$14.50 in the last 10 months, rose to a day high of HK$15.90, but slipped back to close at HK$14.50.
Brokers said clarification of Everbright's interest in Hongkong Telecom could stimulate demand for the share and this could in turn help hold the index above 14,000 this week.
External factors will also be key, brokers said.
"It all depends on what will happen in the United States," said Kenneth Tang, director at Sassoon Securities.
On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 32.91 points, or 0.46 percent, to 7,169.53.

Brokers said this was a cautious rise, after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan defended pre-emptive interest rate hikes against inflation but left the market wondering whether a May hike would materialise.

In the coming week, U.S. wholesale and retail price, industrial production and housing starts reports will be due and with the Fed's May 20 meeting drawing closer, markets could move in choppy patterns, analysts said.
Technically, the Hong Kong market is very vulnerable to bad news.
"The market has been seriously overbought for some time," said Sassoon's Tang. "It looks like we are in a parabolic or exhaustive rise."
Tang said he could not give an upside target for the index, now at a record high, but any retracement would wipe out last week's gains very quickly.
Beijing North Star Co Ltd, the latest H share to enter the market, closed its subcription period on Friday. Dealing in the shares will begin on Wednesday.
